title: ByteDance to Launch AI Agent Targeting Meta's Muse Within Weeks in $70 Billion Bet
summary: ByteDance targets Meta Muse with new AI agent within weeks
detailed: TikTok parent ByteDance will roll out a service similar to Meta's personal AI agent Muse within weeks.
According to Bloomberg on the 12th (local time), ByteDance shared plans for the new agent and mid- to long-term development goals at a recent all-hands meeting of its AI organization.

sentences: TikTok parent ByteDance will roll out a service similar to Meta's personal AI agent Muse within weeks.
Co-founder Zhang Yiming acknowledged the technology gap with leading American AI companies at an internal meeting while signaling his intent to pursue them over the long haul.
According to Bloomberg on the 12th (local time), ByteDance shared plans for the new agent and mid- to long-term development goals at a recent all-hands meeting of its AI organization.

At the private gathering attended by researchers and engineers, Zhang said the company has the capability to compete head-on with OpenAI and Anthropic, but that catching up to frontier technology would take until 2029-2030 at the earliest.
A ByteDance spokesperson did not respond to a request for comment.
The new agent is said to resemble Muse, which Meta unveiled in September.
Muse combines voice conversation with animated avatars to handle tasks on users' behalf.

It keeps running on cloud virtual machines even after users close the app, sending emails, searching for shopping options and making payments, and asks for user confirmation only at critical steps such as transfers or sends.
Meta attracted more than 10 million users in North America within six weeks of launch and is expanding Muse's reach to smart glasses and a dedicated device, the Muse Charm.
Behind ByteDance's move to offer a Muse-like service is a strategy to secure early users by linking the agent to its own platforms.
With massive traffic from TikTok and Douyin, the plan is to attach the agent to existing services and quickly establish it in the market.
ByteDance is said to have run an internal project called Spell since April to integrate personal AI agent capabilities into its mobile assistant Doubao.
It has not been confirmed, however, whether the upcoming agent is directly tied to the Spell project.
The heaviest emphasis in Zhang's remarks was on data.

He lamented that the datasets used by Seed, the company's AI research organization, for large language model (LLM) pretraining are "several orders of magnitude" smaller than those of frontier competitors.
The judgment is that with the scaling law still governing model performance, a data gap translates directly into a ceiling on intelligence.
He also reaffirmed the principle behind the company's technology路线 — its technology roadmap.
ByteDance will focus on in-house R&D rather than relying on distillation, in which smaller models are trained on the outputs of larger ones.

The choice trades short-term benchmark scores for long-term technological competitiveness, and it is not unrelated to the criticism that Chinese majors such as Alibaba, Moonshot and Zhipu have drawn from the U.S. government and Anthropic executives over their use of distillation.
Indeed, Seed's general-purpose language models have not stood out.
Seed 2.1, released in June, remains the last major update to its flagship model even now.
The Seed team itself has acknowledged room for improvement in tackling difficult open-ended tasks and advanced research problems.
Some analysts note that Seed is the only major Chinese AI company that has neither produced a model near the top of global benchmarks nor released model weights externally.
In video generation, by contrast, it holds a clear edge.
It has commercialized the Seedance series, developed on large-scale video data, and is filling the void left by OpenAI's retreat from its AI video service Sora.
ByteDance is said to be weighing investing up to $70 billion (about 93.4 trillion won) to cultivate Seedance as China's top AI video-generation platform.
Reports in August also said the company was pretraining a next-generation model with up to 10 trillion parameters.
It is also pouring resources into talent and organization.

Seed, led by Wu Yonghui, who was recruited from Google DeepMind, is home to about 1,000 researchers and engineers, who are said to receive a separate equity compensation scheme unavailable to other divisions.
Last month it became the first major Chinese AI lab to set up an independent organization dedicated to safety and alignment and hired about 10 core researchers.
The move comes as global competition in AI agents heats up.
Elon Musk's xAI officially launched its pilot Grok Bot on the 11th, and OpenAI released Dots, an agent that carries out work around the clock, in September.
With Meta's Muse off to a strong start, agents have emerged as the next battleground for generative AI.
Market research firm Omdia forecasts that the global AI agent market will grow 30% a year on average from 2025 to 2031.
The figure reflects expectations that monetization paths could widen significantly if agents are combined with existing services such as commerce, advertising and payments.
ByteDance's challenge boils down to a strategy of offsetting its weakness in language models with video, applications and financial firepower.
Zhang is said to be devoting considerable time to setting AI strategy rather than day-to-day management.
The calculation is to seize the market in the near term with agents and video generation while waiting as long as it takes to narrow the data gap in model capability.
For developers, it remains an open question when Seed will release its model weights.
